title: Tanzanian Deep Fried Chicken
community: Urban Tanzania — the street food chicken
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Kuku wa Kukaanga — chicken pieces marinated in Tanzanian spices, coated in seasoned flour, and deep-fried until magnificently golden and crispy. The Tanzanian street food version of fried chicken — spiced with curry powder and cumin rather than KFC's blend.
longDesc: Tanzanian fried chicken is a completely independent development from American fried chicken — the spice blend is Tanzanian (curry powder, cumin, turmeric), the marinade is lemon-based rather than buttermilk, and the result is a distinctly East African flavoured fried chicken of great quality.
equipment: Large deep frying pan or pot
steps: Marinate chicken pieces in all marinade ingredients for 1 hour minimum.
Dredge marinated chicken pieces in seasoned flour — coat thoroughly.
Heat oil to 170°C — enough to submerge the pieces.
Fry in batches — do not crowd.
Fry 12—15 minutes depending on piece size, turning once.
Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately.
chefTips: 170°C is critical — too hot burns crust before chicken cooks; too low produces a greasy result.
Do not crowd the pan — oil temperature drops and chicken steams instead of fries.
cookingScience: See KEN272 for fried chicken cooking science.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: Tanzanian fried chicken at a street food stall is the Friday evening treat — the luxury fast food that working families buy when the week has been good. Its spice profile is unmistakably Tanzanian.
